nodes.text: Smoke and Transportation Safety protocol initiated
Assess safety risks to personnel and public posed by smoke on roads

evidence.source_text: 1. Assess safety risks to personnel and public posed by smoke on roads.

nodes.text: Evaluate potential of smoke to impact roadways up to 10 miles away during initial attack and/or daily sizeup on extended attack

evidence.source_text: During initial attack and/or daily sizeup on extended attack, evaluate the potential of smoke to impact roadways up to 10 miles away.

nodes.text: Identify drainages/topographic features that may allow for smoke to impact roadways during the night and early morning

evidence.source_text: Identify drainages/topographic features that may allow for smoke to impact roadways during the night and early morning.

nodes.text: Monitor key weather variables: Surface Temperature, Relative Humidity, Surface Wind Speed, Cloud Cover

evidence.source_text: 2. Thresholds that, when combined with smoke, indicate potential for reduced roadway visibility.

nodes.text: Mitigate when roadway visibility is expected to be impacted

evidence.source_text:
3. Hazard Control
Mitigate when roadway visibility is expected to be impacted.

nodes.text: Consider use of smoke observers, smoke signs, reduced speed limit, drone car, lead car, lane closure, or entire road closure

evidence.source_text: Depending on thresholds projected and risk assessment, consider use of smoke observers, smoke signs, reduced speed limit, drone car, lead car, lane closure, or, if necessary, entire road closure.

nodes.text: Consider use of local, regional, or national air resource or meteorological specialists (Air Resource Advisors [THSP], Incident Meteorologist [IMET])

evidence.source_text: Consider use of local, regional, or national air resource or meteorological specialists (Air Resource Advisors [THSP], Incident Meteorologist [IMET]).
